Index 2's XRD matches the pyrochlore plus PbO, so it is the Pb-rich absorbing phase. That weakly supports measuring it.

content.text:
I submitted index 2 (Pb 0.68 / Sb 0.32) as the best composition; its EQE was 0.093%, the highest of the three I measured. I used all 3 merit measurements; 2 of the 5 XRD scans went unused.

| Index | Pb / Sb | Phase from XRD | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.68 / 0.32 | Pb₂Sb₂O₇ pyrochlore (Naples yellow) + PbO (similarity 0.80) | **0.093** |
| 0 | 0.72 / 0.28 | not measured (inferred to be the same Pb-rich phases) | 0.036 |
| 11 | 0.40 / 0.60 | not measured (inferred PbSb₂O₆-type) | ~5×10⁻⁶ |

- **Pb-rich side wins.** The yellow pyrochlore absorbs at the 2.4 eV illumination and gave the only useful response. The Sb-rich side is about 20,000× worse.
- **Sb-rich side is a wide-gap phase.** XRD at indices 8 and 14 matched PbSb₂O₆ best, though only weakly (similarity 0.42 at index 8). MEGNet puts its gap at 2.7 eV, above the photon energy, which fits the near-zero EQE.
- **The peak is probably near index 2.** Moving further Pb-rich to index 0 cut EQE by more than half. Indices 1 and 3–7 were never measured, so a composition slightly Sb-richer than index 2 could do better.
- **The ML models were not much use.** MEGNet predicted about 0 eV for the pyrochlore and 3.36 eV for PbO, both at odds with measured gaps. The choices were driven by XRD and the measured EQE trend instead.
